scope: T-69/T-76 authoritative billing outbox and delivery slice only; neither full ticket is declared complete.

order: Existing billing tables, Supabase auth.uid(), roles and reviewed RLS
Approved maintenance window: quiesce every billing writer and drain in-flight transactions before acquiring receipt, entitlement and audit write locks
COMMIT delivers NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'; verify the actual PostgREST schema reload and named-argument RPC binding before resuming billing writers
Verified billing writers using apply_billing_event; analytics collection and delivery remain OFF
Deploy the matching deliver-analytics payload validator with its environment gate OFF; complete every activation gate before separately enabling collection, delivery or scheduling
preflight: Retain every export, schema, legacy-receipt reconciliation and writer-rollout gate from billing-rollout.json.

Check that apply_billing_event has the expected ten-argument signature, owner, empty search_path and service-only permissions. Check existing dependencies, grants, triggers, default privileges and audit defaults on the actual database.

Fresh installation only. Any existing analytics installation, private billing wrapper or finish_analytics_delivery signature requires a separately reviewed forward migration. Never DROP an old acknowledgement signature, erase its queue or replay this file as an upgrade or downgrade.

Measure billing_events size, index-build duration, disk/WAL headroom and lock contention in isolated staging. analytics_prior_captures and analytics_prior_refunds are non-CONCURRENTLY indexes built inside this transaction; the explicit write locks block billing writes until COMMIT. An approved maintenance window with all writers quiesced is mandatory.

The 5s lock_timeout aborts on lock-acquisition waits; it is not an index-build or total-downtime limit. On failure, roll back the complete transaction and reassess the maintenance window. Do not force through blocking sessions.

The migration preserves the original billing function under a private name and wraps the original public signature. Its prior service_role execute grant is revoked. No application writer may bypass the public wrapper.

The transactional NOTIFY requests schema reload only after a successful COMMIT. An actual PostgREST cache refresh and service-only named-argument calls must be verified separately; local PGlite is not PostgREST.
All billing writers must already use the verified RPC; direct legacy entitlement/audit writers are not covered. This task neither deploys nor edits those handlers.
migration.acknowledgement_signature: public.finish_analytics_delivery(p_event_id uuid, p_lease_token uuid, p_outcome text, p_error text DEFAULT NULL)
migration.atomicity: An accepted original billing transaction and eligible outbox insert commit or roll back together. Failed outbox inserts are not swallowed. Duplicate, skipped, stale-reference and out-of-order receipts never emit an event.
migration.history: No migration backfill. Existing billing audits suppress previously seen canonical charge/refund aliases even if consent or collection was previously off. Suppressed events are never resurrected on regrant.
migration.rollback_policy: Pause the scheduler, SQL collection/delivery gates and edge environment gate. Eligible admitted backlog survives an off/on cycle: pauses do not suppress pending/retry work and the pause trigger releases claimed but not authorized leases without consuming an attempt, including an interrupted sixth claim. Pre-send authorization also releases a paused lease; authorized in-flight outcomes can still be acknowledged. Collection disabled means no new analytics admission; its new enablement epoch fences late arrivals from the paused period, not previously admitted rows. Billing receipt/audit/entitlement writes continue unchanged. Do not change consent policy or source attestation as a pause mechanism. Leave the wrapper and queue intact; never drop RPC signatures, undo RLS, erase financial history, reseed cursors or revoke historical access.

pricing_and_access.historical_promises: Unchanged. No new expiry, automatic renewal, offer end, price lock revocation or coaching promise is introduced.
pricing_and_access.price_class: Always other_or_unknown: neither INR 100 nor a current catalog-looking amount proves an effective nominal/standard assignment. Existing payment notes and client flags cannot supply an assignment.
pricing_and_access.charge_kind: Always unknown until authoritative charge-kind assignments are available. Active access, trials and checkout completion are never payment evidence.
pricing_and_access.financial_interpretation: These are captured/processed amounts only, not customers, recognized revenue, MRR, profit, bank cash or complete reconciled totals. No observed financial metric was collected.

source_provenance.rail_authority: Derive actual rail from signed payload.payment.entity.method: upi, card, netbanking or wallet; missing, non-scalar and all other values become unknown. Refunds inherit the stored purchase rail. A generic checkout intention does not prove the actual payment method.
source_provenance.measurement_contract_gate: The parent-owned office/measurement-contract.json is unchanged. Its owner must reconcile the actual-rail enum with any generic checkout-intent rail before activation, retaining separate meanings rather than mislabelling netbanking/wallet/unknown as upi or card.
source_provenance.authority: Only the service-role verified billing writer may call the RPC. SQL does not itself verify provider signatures or fetch provider objects; those checks remain in the existing webhook.
source_provenance.mode_limit: The existing Razorpay RPC payload does not carry the writer's key mode. A reviewed database owner must explicitly attest analytics_billing_sources.account_id, billing_mode and verified_at for a dedicated live-only writer/database. This configuration is an operational trust prerequisite, NOT automatic proof of live mode. A matching account_id alone cannot distinguish test and live payments.
source_provenance.isolation_gate: Do not enable a source until keys, webhook secret, provider account, database and absence of sandbox/mixed writers are independently verified together. Never point test and live writers at this same attested ledger. Reverification after key/mode/account changes is mandatory; source activation epochs invalidate old queued work.
source_provenance.defaults: No source rows are provisioned. Source mode defaults unknown and enabled defaults false. Test/unknown/disabled sources, explicit test markers, unknown accounts, missing proof fields and malformed monetary values produce no outbox record.
source_provenance.canonical_identity: Private SHA-256 keys namespace the signed provider payment/refund identifier by account, provider, live mode and entity kind. Each outbox row also has a unique receipt foreign key and a random immutable event UUID. Provider/member identifiers are not exported.
source_provenance.timestamp_contract: Analytics uses the signed created_at whole second. A fractional p_occurred_at within that same second is normalized for analytics only; billing receives its original exact timestamp. Different signed seconds are rejected for analytics. Consent/global/source time boundaries are checked against the signed second, so fractional RPC precision cannot move a pre-consent event across a grant boundary. Same-second boundary uncertainty can conservatively exclude an event.
source_provenance.refunds: Require a newly accepted processed receipt with its own current consent revision/version/time, linked to a retained purchase of the same owner/source/reference and sufficient remaining refundable amount. The parent purchase is historical amount/tier/rail evidence, not the refund's consent grant. Delivered or suppressed purchases may support a newly consented refund after revoke/regrant or policy renewal; neither an old purchase nor an old suppressed refund is revived or resent. Preserve the original tier, rail and price class. Dedupe each refund identity; cumulative rows, including suppressed/dead refunds, cannot exceed the capture.

consent.scope: Separate server billing analytics only. It is not consent to legacy SDK activity or the two existing in-memory client diagnostics.
consent.identity: Authenticated auth.uid() only; no client-supplied owner or timestamp argument. The server records policy version, capture time and opaque revision. Repeated grant of the current active version is idempotent.
consent.grant: A grant must name the current server policy. Collection also requires the separate global/source approvals; consent alone does not activate anything.
consent.revoke: A denial/revoke accepts even an outdated policy label and invalidates pending, retry, leased and sending rows. Regrant never revives them. Policy changes require a new grant.
consent.delivery_check: Claim and immediate pre-HTTP authorization require current consent/source eligibility plus both operational gates. Acknowledgement records the outcome of an already-authorized attempt even during a pause. Loss of consent/source eligibility makes the row terminally suppressed but cannot erase send evidence. Owner consent changes and per-event authorization/acknowledgement serialize through the same transaction advisory lock.
consent.in_flight_limit: Once pre-HTTP authorization commits, revocation cannot recall a request already begun or reliably close the interval before remote send. A revoked sending row retains delivery_authorized_at, last_error=in_flight_ineligible and its original token solely for one late acknowledgement, even after lease expiry; it cannot be authorized, reclaimed or revived by regrant. provider_acknowledged_at records a locally recognized positive response, not durable ingestion. Missing acknowledgement remains ambiguous, never proof of never-sent. Suppression after authorization returns uncertain/HTTP 503, not skipped success. Tokens are cleared after acknowledgement. Previously delivered provider data is not deleted; billing audit sources and historical payment/access records are untouched.
consent.client_integration: Not implemented within the permitted files. The existing Track.setMeasurementConsent checkbox neither grants nor revokes this server consent. Do not activate until a separately reviewed account-aware UI calls these RPCs and withdrawal/retention handling is approved.

dispatcher.environment_gate: ANALYTICS_DELIVERY_ENABLED must equal the exact string true; unset, false and other spellings are inert. SQL collection/delivery gates and source/owner consent must also permit the event.
dispatcher.authentication: Dedicated 32-512 character non-whitespace scheduler secret in Authorization: Bearer, compared through SHA-256 digests. It must not equal the service-role key. Requests cannot select a destination, event payload or batch size.
dispatcher.gateway_gate: An approved future deployment must configure the function gateway to accept the dedicated scheduler token, for example verify_jwt=false only for this function, then test its own unauthorized denial. No gateway or deployment configuration is changed here.
dispatcher.supabase_origin: An environment-configured HTTPS *.supabase.co origin without a path, query, credentials or port. Local/custom domains are deliberately unsupported by the deployed transport.
dispatcher.secret_handling: PostHog ingestion key comes only from the environment. Service-role credentials go only to the configured Supabase RPC origin. All redirects are disabled; bodies, secrets, identifiers and exception messages are never logged or returned.
dispatcher.retry_policy: Network/body timeouts, missing positive provider acknowledgement, HTTP 408/425/429 and 5xx retry with min(3600, 30 * 2^(attempts-1)) seconds backoff. Permanent HTTP/schema failures and six failed or abandoned attempts terminate in dead. No automatic unbounded requeue.
dispatcher.lease_policy: Service-only SKIP LOCKED claims return UUID/token pairs. Authorization consumes a live lease once. Expired active leases can be reclaimed with a new token and the same event UUID; wrong or superseded tokens are rejected. The only late-ack exception is the original retained token on an already-suppressed sending row: it records evidence without enabling any send, retry or unsuppression.
dispatcher.provider_semantics: Bounded at-least-once attempts, NOT exactly-once external HTTP. The internal delivered state and provider_acknowledged_at mean the configured local HTTP/body predicate passed, not that PostHog durably ingested the event. A lost acknowledgement may repeat HTTP; stable uuid/$insert_id are requested dedupe identifiers whose real behavior is unverified. A positive response after revocation is stored on a suppressed row for reconciliation and reported uncertain. Never claim provider deduplication, persistence or measurement completeness from these fixtures.
dispatcher.deployment_coupling: SQL authorization emits exactly seven property keys; captureBody rejects different arity, extra/missing keys and unrecognized enum values. SQL, dispatcher, rail enums and parent measurement definitions are a coupled release. Keep scheduler plus SQL/environment gates OFF, deploy the matching dispatcher and verify exact SQL-to-wire fixtures before any activation. An old upi-only dispatcher dead-letters new rail values; any future property addition/removal requires a coordinated forward migration and dispatcher deployment, not an independent SQL rollout.
dispatcher.identity_and_properties: Only tier, rail, currency, amount_minor, price_class, billing_mode and charge_kind, plus event-scoped distinct_id/$insert_id UUIDs and false person-profile/disabled-GeoIP controls. No member uid, provider IDs, name, email, health, report/reason content, URLs or free text. Event-scoped identity deliberately cannot supply member cohorts or distinct buyer counts.
dispatcher.operational_limits: No scheduler, alerting, operator replay tool, provider deletion or retention purge is installed. Dead/suppressed rows need an approved operational policy; preserve canonical dedupe history. The remote provider necessarily sees dispatcher transport metadata, not the member's IP.

provider_acknowledgement.local_predicate: HTTP 2xx and JSON number 1, or a JSON object with numeric status equal to 1. These are provisional local formats, not externally proven success semantics. Textual status Ok, string 1, booleans and malformed responses are not accepted without evidence and a reviewed code change.
provider_acknowledgement.documentation_evidence: Read-only fetches succeeded. The official page documents /i/v0/e/ and /batch/, anonymous $process_person_profile=false, top-level distinct_id for single events and properties.distinct_id in batch examples. Its Invalid events section says HTTP 200 can accompany dropped events because processing is asynchronous. The fetched pages do not specify the positive JSON body shapes for the configured /capture/ endpoint.
provider_acknowledgement.not_established: No provider request was made. Compatibility of legacy /capture/, its actual acknowledgement body, properties.distinct_id on this single-event endpoint, top-level uuid/$insert_id dedupe, $ip:null/$geoip_disable handling and durable ingestion remain unobserved.
provider_acknowledgement.required_evidence: Before activation, separately authorize designated noncustomer integration fixtures and record selected region/endpoint response shapes, negative responses, durable event observation, duplicate identity behavior and privacy-property handling. A documentation fetch or green mock is not sufficient. Keep all gates OFF until the actual contract is demonstrated.

retention.parent_purchase_dependency: Refund normalization requires the original analytics_outbox purchase row and linked billing_event_receipts reference even when the purchase is delivered, suppressed or dead. Never purge a parent while refunds may still arrive. A retention design must first preserve minimal authoritative parent amount/tier/rail/source/reference bindings, canonical dedupe and receipts through an approved refund/dispute horizon and late-delivery window, or replace the lookup with a reviewed durable source.
retention.refund_sum_dependency: All child refund rows, including suppressed/dead rows, contribute to the cumulative amount bound. Purging them without an authoritative retained aggregate reopens refunded capacity and invalidates the guard. Preserve the dependency or replace it transactionally before any purge.
retention.billing_audit_dependency: billing_events supplies prior canonical payment/refund alias detection, including occurrences during collection-off or consent-off periods. Analytics suppression never removes or rewrites the payment audit source, receipts or entitlements. Audit retention is a separate payment/privacy policy, not an analytics rollback.
retention.growth_limit: Growth is currently unbounded. No retention horizon, purge, archive replacement or provider deletion workflow is approved or installed. Resolve this dependency and withdrawal handling before activation; no invented retention period or completeness claim.

unsupported_or_incomplete: Lemon Squeezy currently supplies subscription access state, not normalized charges/refunds; it emits no monetary analytics here.
Razorpay subscription activation/resume/charged events are access-only in the current writer and do not emit purchases here.

The SQL normalizer can represent individually accepted partial processed refunds, but the unchanged webhook ignores partial refunds before the RPC. Complete partial-refund analytics needs a separately scoped upstream billing change.

Refunds rejected by the existing reference cursor after a newer purchase and pre-migration/unconsented purchases are not reconstructed. This accepted-event stream is not a complete financial ledger or refund reconciliation feed.

Collection pauses stop new admission, and consent-off events are not backfilled from their payment audits. A newly consented refund may exist without an externally delivered parent purchase; suppressed purchases and old refunds are never resurrected. Parent/child retention dependencies and conservative same-second time boundaries further limit completeness.

PostHog acknowledgement formats, /capture/ compatibility, ingestion, deduplication and privacy-property behavior are unverified blocking gates. The parent owner must reconcile actual payment rails with the untouched measurement contract before activation.
Effective nominal/standard price assignments, charge-kind assignments, staff/internal-QA exclusion cohorts, bank settlements and completeness watermarks are not implemented.

Server consent UI/revocation integration, member-level cohort linkage, registration/activation/new-workout events and reporting are not implemented. The measurement contract and board remain unchanged.

findings_fixed: Actual payment methods map to upi/card/netbanking/wallet or unknown in SQL and the strict dispatcher allowlist; refunds inherit the actual rail.

Collection/delivery pauses preserve eligible admitted backlog and release unsent leases without consuming attempts; in-flight outcomes survive a pause. An interrupted sixth claim was reproduced failing, then fixed by releasing unsent leases in the pause trigger.
A new refund uses its own current consent revision/version after revoke/regrant without resending a delivered or suppressed purchase or an old refund.

The fresh-install migration declares writer-order locks, a 5s lock-wait limit, non-concurrent index maintenance requirements and transactional PostgREST schema reload. Existing acknowledgement signatures are refused, never dropped or replaced.

Revoked in-flight work retains minimal authorization/positive-response evidence and an acknowledgement-only token; the dispatcher reports post-send suppression as uncertain, not skipped. Payment audits remain unchanged.
PostHog acknowledgement/dedupe assertions are replaced with an explicit unverified activation blocker and an accurate account of the official documentation evidence; no live verification is claimed.
Parent-purchase, child-refund sum and billing-audit retention dependencies are explicit, including the unbounded-growth and no-purge limitation.
Exact payload arity and enum deployment coupling are explicit; SQL/dispatcher and parent measurement compatibility must be verified together with every gate OFF.

Fractional RPC timestamps normalize to the signed provider second for analytics without changing billing timestamps or crossing consent boundaries. Missing payment entities and non-INR monetary inputs are tested.
Existing strict scalar validation still rejects array-shaped names, tiers and rails before HTTP. A misplaced migration patch was caught by immediate SQL tests, repaired and rerun successfully.
review.independent_review: The complete user-supplied independent review was read and its findings addressed locally. Independent re-review of these fixes remains pending; no subagents or fallback models were used.
